questions.question: In infectious disease transmission, what is a vector?
choices: An immune cell that produces antibodies
An organism that carries a pathogen between hosts
A molecule recognized by an antibody
A genetic change that protects every host

questions.question: Which structure is part of the body's first barrier against infection?
choices: Bone marrow
Pancreas
Skin
Thyroid gland

questions.question: Which cells are central to many immune defenses?
choices: Red blood cells
Fat cells
Muscle cells
White blood cells

questions.question: What is an antigen?
choices: A molecular feature recognized by immune receptors
An enzyme that digests all microbes
A sugar used only by red blood cells
A hormone that controls body height

questions.question: What do antibodies bind to?
choices: Any nutrient equally
Specific antigens
Only oxygen molecules
Every body cell indiscriminately

questions.question: Which response is part of innate immunity?
choices: Production of memory cells after a specific infection
A faster response to a previously encountered antigen
Inflammation near damaged tissue
A response tailored to one vaccine antigen

questions.question: Which immune cells can develop into antibody-secreting cells?
choices: Red blood cells
Platelets
Skin cells
B cells

questions.question: How does adaptive immunity differ from innate immunity?
choices: It can develop antigen-specific memory
It relies only on the outer skin
It responds identically to every substance
It cannot distinguish molecular features

questions.question: Why can a second exposure to the same antigen produce a faster immune response?
choices: The pathogen always becomes harmless with age
Memory cells formed during the first response remain
All body cells turn into antibodies
The skin permanently blocks that antigen

questions.question: How do vaccines generally prepare adaptive immunity?
choices: They permanently replace white blood cells
They supply antibiotics against every virus
They expose the immune system to a harmless form or component of a pathogen
They remove all microbes from the body

questions.question: Why are antibiotics not generally effective against viral infections?
choices: Viruses are simply smaller bacterial species
Viruses reproduce only outside cells
Antibiotics strengthen viral cell walls
They target bacterial features that viruses do not have

questions.question: What is the main concern with antibiotic resistance?
choices: Bacteria with resistance can survive treatment and reproduce
Resistance makes all bacteria more sensitive to treatment
Resistance stops bacteria from reproducing
Resistance arises only after all bacteria are killed

questions.question: What occurs in an autoimmune disorder?
choices: Immune defenses respond only to harmless outside substances
Immune defenses attack the body's own tissues
The body fails to make any red blood cells
Bacterial toxins digest the skin before immune activation

questions.question: Why does washing hands help reduce some infections?
choices: It builds antigen-specific memory against every microbe
It kills every microbe on the skin permanently
It removes microbes that could be transferred to others
It replaces the skin's need for immune cells

questions.question: How does an infectious disease differ from a noninfectious disease?
choices: An infectious disease must cause a fever
A noninfectious disease cannot involve genes
A noninfectious disease always affects only one organ
An infectious disease results from a transmissible biological agent

questions.question: In a bacterial population, a few cells already resist an antibiotic. What does treatment tend to do?
choices: Favor survival and reproduction of resistant cells
Eliminate resistance from the surviving population
Favor sensitive cells over resistant cells
Make resistance equally common regardless of survival

questions.question: An antibody binds antigen X but not antigen Y. What does this demonstrate?
choices: Equal binding to all antigens
Specific molecular recognition
Loss of immune memory
Conversion of antigens into white blood cells

questions.question: Two groups encounter the same pathogen; one group has relevant immune memory. What response is generally expected in that group?
choices: No possibility of infection under any conditions
A complete absence of innate responses
A quicker antigen-specific defense
Immediate production of new red blood cell types

questions.question: A community has fewer susceptible hosts after vaccination. How can this help others?
choices: It ensures every person has identical antibodies
It makes pathogens stop evolving
It turns all infections into noninfectious diseases
It can reduce opportunities for pathogen transmission

questions.question: A scientist compares antibodies before and after antigen exposure. Which result supports an adaptive response?
choices: An increase in antibodies that recognize that antigen
An increase in antibodies recognizing only unrelated antigens
A change in blood volume without antigen-specific recognition
A fall in relevant antibody levels with no other response
